# Current Goal: Practical Independent Lifting and Windows Program Delivery

The practical DX-Ball Windows lifting goal is complete within the documented
comparison and runtime scope. The [delivery review](dxball-windows-lift-delivery.md)
records the source archive, application inventory, normal-program evidence and
explicit fidelity limits. The final inventory accounts for the 190 selected
operations, private helpers, startup zeroing and switch data; it found no missing
application subsystem in the reviewed span. Five one-byte boundary endpoint
corrections pass all 41 affected local cases. Application C and the delivered
source archive are unchanged. Historical scratch values on failed API calls or
malformed assets, unsupported unsafe addresses and arbitrary concurrency remain
limitations; reproducing every such history is not a prerequisite for this
practical delivery. This completion does not grant strong qualification or claim
readiness for every Win32 target.

The current DX-Ball delivery target remains a **Windows executable built from
the lifted C**, using Win32, DirectDraw, DirectSound and WinMM through explicit
adapters. Readable application C does not require replacing those operating-system
services. Prioritize the Windows assembly's behavior, adapter/state correspondence,
normal execution and usable source-project handoff. The operator clarified on
2026-09-29 that porting the lifted C away from Windows runtimes is **outside this
project's scope**. Windows execution through Wine is the preferred test path.
Earlier other-platform delivery requirements below are historical and do not
control current completion. Existing cross-architecture consumer results remain
useful evidence, not a required porting campaign. The initial SDL graphics
prototype was deferred on 2026-09-29 and the
Windows assembly recipe restored exactly; it is retained only under
`build/dxball-portable-desktop-2026-09-29/deferred-prototype/`, with no delivery claim.

The Windows continuation now exercises all five scenes through normal program
entry. The same external workload drives original and C candidates into the
editor, clears/saves boards and navigates between them. Their complete 20,000-byte
board files and three visible editor images match. Clearing two boards through
the editor then exercises gameplay, end-of-board cleanup, score display, score
table and return to menu. The score images and saved board/score files match;
the returned animated menus differ in their moving dots and ball. These are
wall-clock observations, not a deterministic rendering claim. No component or
state-binding correction was needed for these paths.

A clean source handoff now builds outside the repository using only Make,
MinGW-w64 and its resource compiler. The public apply builds it in 2.54 seconds
and runs the score workload. The missing embedded icon is now retained as two
ordinary Windows resource payloads; all payload bytes, IDs and languages match
the pinned image. Adding those resources leaves every preceding executable
section unchanged. The source archive contains 1,107 files, including 46 assets,
with no executable, compiled object or original image. Extracting it and building
again produces identical section bytes. `WINDOWS.md` gives build/run and local
edit instructions. All 49 component sources and evidence are unchanged.
Evidence and the source archive are under
`build/dxball-program-scenes-windows-2026-09-29/` (`validation.json`,
`dxball-windows-source.tar.gz`). Repository metadata, Python lint and format
registry checks pass. The later delivery review above accounts for the remaining
application inventory and records the unsupported status/scratch-history paths
as explicit limits on the practical translation.

The standalone Windows MIDI adapter now preserves provider updates between C
calls. A local check reproduced two losses in the preceding adapter: overwriting
a queue link and overwriting updated flags while the C view remained unchanged.
The adapter now publishes only C changes, deriving its write baseline from the
same captured header as the view. Initial private header bytes come from the
owned parser allocation. The stream component C is unchanged.

Seven SDK-adapter checks pass through the existing shared Wine environment,
including actual native completion, reset and callback requeue, plus controlled
provider updates and open failure. All callbacks finish and pending counts reach
zero before release in these cases. Native reset/requeue checks retain the original
ignored `STILLPLAYING` unprepare results; close subsequently returns the buffers.
The backend sees candidate calls and object identities only. These are finite
adapter/lifecycle checks, not an exhaustive concurrency or device-failure claim.
The public apply also passes normal game execution (gameplay, brick removal,
10 points and clean exit). All 647 exported component files, 50 component objects
and the 49-component selection remain unchanged; among 120 preceding assembly/
bridge/backend objects only `program-win32-midi.o` changes. No pilot or solver
work is needed. Evidence: `build/dxball-program-midi-2026-09-29/validation.json`.

The [source-program integration audit](dxball-standalone-integration.md) now
separates remaining native application bodies, program-owned state and service
bindings, CRT adapters and platform backends. The 49-component selection now
links into a normal-entry PE32 `dxball.exe` using the Win32 SDK, owned C state and
packaged assets. It executes title, menu and gameplay and exits normally without
loading the original executable. The public `candidate apply` path builds and
runs that source program. This is a first executable integration milestone, not
whole-game equivalence or completion on another platform. The
[worklist](../tests/fixtures/dxball-standalone/README.md) records reproduction and
the remaining platform, observation and historical-memory obligations.

The first assembly layer now constructs program-owned objects using the existing
component types, named initial data extracted from the pinned image, and direct
C startup connections. Its startup check matches retained native scores, boards
and all initialized numeric samples on x86-64 and emulated AArch64. Shared board,
score and table views refer to the same owners; a second program instance remains
independent. The executable loads neither the original image nor the workbench.
All 49 preceding component implementations, records and compiled objects are
retained. The public apply workflow adds the assembly without another pilot build.

Scene assembly connects the five-scene dispatch table, title animation, text,
palette, damage, board storage, editor regions and rendering. Gameplay and audio
assembly now add 194 further service connections through the existing motion,
brick, pickup, particle, explosion, powerup, progression, cleanup and audio units.
Typed allocations use ordinary malloc/free without zeroing payloads. Including MDS
resources, the preceding assembly resolved 377 declared bindings. The remaining
143 are now connected through resource/byte adapters and actual Win32 services;
the full PE32 link succeeds. All component implementations and records remain unchanged.

MDS resource assembly now connects music records, the existing loader/parser/event
chain, owned C storage and immutable file input. All six bundled music files
match retained native metadata and used event bytes in both file and memory
modes on x86-64 and emulated AArch64. The 12 cases exercise 376 buffers and
1,513,032 event bytes, including owner links and input released before output
observation. Host ASan/UBSan/leak checks also pass. This adds 26 service bindings
without component changes or new workbench mechanisms. The stdio adapter covers
packaged immutable assets, not general Win32 file semantics; malformed inputs,
allocation failure histories and MIDI playback remain outside this assembly check.

menu binding mistakenly used single-page damage. It now uses the original
mirrored-page operation; score-screen damage remains single-page. Fourteen
routing checks exercise that distinction, and reintroducing the old menu error
fails locally. No component algorithm correction or new workbench mechanism was
needed. Original source was not consulted.

comparisons still pass and another program owner's state remains untouched.
All 49 components, 161 preceding component/consumer objects and 56 subsystem
binaries are retained on each architecture. The public apply checks reuse the

End-to-end tests must not be the sole way to expose a supported class of semantic
errors. Reduce each discovered discrepancy to a retained component, boundary or
runtime-service regression, using a small connected consumer when state or
lifecycle spans operations. Inability to express or execute that regression
without the full application is a tooling gap. Missing test inputs remain a
coverage gap; finite tests do not establish a universal guarantee. This requirement
keeps the workflow useful for targets whose complete execution cannot be automated.

## Default workflow: practical stateful lifting

The operator's 2026-09-21 review changed the implementation order. The delivered
[P1–P4 in the mandatory plan](whole-target-independent-lifting.md#practical-subsystem-milestone-and-sequencing)
milestone covers a substantial connected subsystem that operators can define,
author, compare, debug and integrate, followed by reuse on a structurally different
target. Its completion does not depend on formal closure of G1–G7; those remain
the separate stronger qualification exits. Publish usable experimental
checkpoints as they become executable, with their tested scope and assumptions.
The earlier goal's comparison/lowercase pair is an achieved intermediate
gate; the mandatory plan's practical sequencing determines the next work.

The selected scope starts with **jq array storage and lifetime beneath the
value/path network**, followed by DX-Ball's connected resource lifecycle. Creation,
retain/release, shared reads, copy-on-write mutation, growth and destruction are
implemented by authored C in the bounded jq scope. The native-`jv` transport and
leak observer alone would not supply that implementation. Retained outside-scope
services and representation readers remain explicit. DX-Ball now extends beyond
the early-failure experiment into normal continuation and a resource consumer.

The normal workflow is boundary definition -> ordinary C -> retained/generated
comparison -> discrepancy replay and repair -> real-consumer integration -> reuse.
Use existing interfaces, service catalogs, generated bridges, C adapters, comparison
packages, SDK and experimental build/test commands. Formal checks are optional
additional evidence. Current experimental policy already supports unavailable or
timed-out proofs; missing executable transport or known behavioral discrepancies
remain separate problems. Keep tested, assumed and proved findings distinct.

Acceptance requires shared-alias/lifetime/allocation-failure negatives, accurate
local versus integration invalidation, a compatible representation change, and
both public target walkthroughs without new proof machinery for each unit.
Measure operator effort and warm edit/diagnosis time alongside separate phase
costs. Retained cases and small fixtures precede pilot rebuilds. No new unrestricted
quoting proof attempt is the immediate next action; the results below are retained
strong-assurance work and diagnostics, not practical-milestone prerequisites.

The selected P1–P4 implementation and execution exits are delivered below.
The practical delivery goal is complete in the audited scopes; full qualification is tracked separately.
Repository validation for the newest checkpoint is recorded with its evidence.

### Operator/program handoff

The 2026-09-22 priority review replaces the open-ended queue of additional native
dependencies with a bounded **operator handoff and program execution** milestone.
The [H1–H3 acceptance criteria](whole-target-independent-lifting.md#h1h3-operator-handoff-and-program-execution)
control this delivered milestone. P1–P4 are delivered within their stated scopes; neither more
component counts nor completion of broader formal proofs is the next exit.

1. **H1: reproduce and establish a new boundary.** Make the existing connected Hello setup
   reproducible from pinned original/runtime inputs and supported authoring APIs,
   without a previous developer's completed comparison directory. Demonstrate
   boundary definition, ordinary C editing, memory/service discrepancy replay,
   repair, unaffected-neighbor reuse and experimental build/run. Record manual
   adapter work and any tool-internal changes; package editing alone is insufficient.
   Fresh reproduction and the [previously unprepared string-conversion trial](../tests/fixtures/hello-string-conversion/README.md)
   now pass using documented facilities; analysis/adapter/setup effort is measured
   separately from warm edits. Requiring checker, artifact or compiler internals changes
   is a tooling gap. An agent-run trial is not an independent human usability study.
   Its workspace must expose inputs, shared objects, services, outcomes, examples
   and assumptions through reusable shared layouts/lifecycle conventions.
2. **H2: run through the program.** Carry that selected subsystem through Hello's
   normal program entry and representative command-line workloads, observing which
   selected allocation/conversion operations run and including error paths. Original
   startup/TLS and retained services need explicit executable treatment. The
   [normal-entry recipe](../tests/fixtures/hello-program/README.md) now delivers
   the selected twelve-workload handoff, including actual TLS execution, output
   defects, retained replay and repair. The routine-image suite remains separate.
   Keep this an experimental mixed implementation. The practical path continues
   to standalone source, reusable platform backends and another architecture;
   strong admission remains a separate claim.
3. **H3: check that the facilities transfer.** Reproduce the connected DX-Ball
   workflow from fresh inputs with the same authoring/runtime facilities, and use
   the jq network for affected shared-state regressions. Document target-specific
   adapters and unsupported interactions. Fresh DX-Ball reproduction and the jq
   regression now pass. The controlled graphics oracle remains
   explicitly distinct from native DirectDraw execution.

The handoff is complete within these scopes. Freeze further component expansion
while closing concrete standalone/runtime usability gaps. Further
operations must close a concrete standalone-source dependency, selected workload,
missing executable interaction or demonstrated discrepancy. Optimize a measured setup/edit/replay
cost when it impedes that sequence. Finish the operator sequence after each shared
fix; do not turn the fix into a universal heap, callback or proof-model project.

H1–H3 complete when their recorded workflows and integration runs pass, even if
formal rules are unavailable or time out under the existing experimental policy.
Known discrepancies, unsupported execution and stale inputs still prevent a pass.
The practical whole-program goal remains open until its standalone-source,
reusable-backend, cross-architecture and validation exits are satisfied. Strong
qualification does not control practical completion; it keeps its own G1–G7 exits.
Tested, assumed, unobserved and proved findings remain separate throughout.

## Implementation sequence and required exits

### G1. Establish retained inputs and a supported authoring profile

- Inspect current implementations, retained artifacts and dirty-tree ownership
  before changes. Record the baseline and existing failures; old statuses alone
  are insufficient evidence. Reuse small Metapad fixtures for fast regression.
- Select and record a real jq operation with a loop, mutable shared values and
  multiple dependency operations/caller contexts. Record exact original inputs,
  entries/exits, original-side oracle, boundary, relevant object aliases/lifetimes,
  executable adapters and unresolved assumptions. Do not select a trivial renamed
  fixture merely to avoid the intended interaction shape.
- Start from the current restricted standard-C profile. Document the supported
  subset and provide generated headers/helpers, compiler/editor configuration,
  examples and source-located actionable diagnostics. Make allocation/state/service
  helpers available only with implemented executable meanings.
- Separate dialect conformance, executable transport, practical comparison and
  proof-rule applicability. Demonstrate valid supported C that remains locally
  testable although the required formal composition rule is unavailable.

### G2. Deliver the public edit, compare and replay loop

- Extend existing component/boundary commands, SDK and work packages to prepare
  one concrete driver invoking original and authored implementations. Pinned real
  dependencies are acceptable initially; bind and display their exact versions.
- Construct independent original/source states preserving logical aliases,
  relevant contents and lifetimes. Compare declared outcomes, memory and service
  observations at the relevant interaction points. Record unavailable observation
  capabilities and the distinction between recovered-C and native-original oracles.
- On the real jq consumer, introduce a meaningful bug, retain a replayable case,
  show the first divergence, repair ordinary C and rerun through public tools.
  Exercise shared-value and error/failure cases. No routine manual digest editing,
  handwritten generated-model edits or per-component production Python/Nix phase.
  Explicit reusable test fixture C is permitted.

### G3. Demonstrate dependency isolation and accurate invalidation

- Replace one significant real dependency with controlled responses that validate
  arguments and relevant current state before supplying outcomes and writes.
  Establish absence of its body from that local execution and generated harness.
- Edit that supplier under unchanged contract meaning. Reuse unchanged isolated
  consumer evidence with zero consumer execution/model/compiler/solver work;
  independently check the supplier and rerun affected real-dependency integration.
  Comparisons which executed its old body must become stale. Report actual work.
- Refine a consumed boundary without changing its signature and invalidate the
  affected checks. Retain excluded counterexamples when narrowing a domain.
  Deliberately violate a dependency assumption and expose the applicability or
  integration failure. Reuse an existing supported formal proof alongside the
  practical results without conflating their authority.

### G4. Build and run the experimental configuration

- Introduce a distinct typed experimental execution manifest/policy and share
  existing build/link/runner operations beneath the admission boundaries. Account
  for both outer suite and per-case native-realization gates. Do not fabricate
  qualification fields or reinterpret existing strong receipts.
- Bind selected implementations, adapters, runtime, accepted assumptions, required
  checks and actual linked binary. Check executable transport, symbol/ownership
  consistency and representation compatibility. Persist experimental assumptions
  in project policy so normal edits do not require repeated confirmation.
- Run the selected real jq component network. An unsupported proof and bounded
  proof timeout must not block an otherwise eligible experimental run. A known
  mismatch remains a failure; diagnostic replay is not passing readiness.
- Reject stale binary/input bindings and reject experimental manifests at all
  affected strong-authority entry points. Label the executed scope precisely;
  a component-network driver is not full jq or portable application completion.

### G5. Check generalization with a second real interaction shape

- Apply the same public workflow to a retained DX-Ball lifecycle consumer with a
  real failure/cleanup sequence or a supported callback schedule. Name the actual
  sequence, observation scope and remaining unsupported behaviors.
- Use shared fixture/adapter capabilities instead of copying target-specific
  orchestration. Demonstrate one bounded private representation change on either
  network, compare its logical observations, and reject an incompatible mixed
  selection. Preserve the distinction between components and replacement groups.
- Keep this a concrete generalization check. General concurrency, arbitrary
  callback capture and a universal Win32/heap model are not prerequisites.

### G6. Validate and publish reproducible completion evidence locally

- Exercise negative controls for broken alias cloning, missing observations,
  wrong service arguments/order, lifetime errors, invalid or empty setup,
  boundary exclusions, stale evidence and false qualification. Separate harness
  failures, behavioral mismatches, violated assumptions and unavailable checks.
- Record preparation, compilation, model, solver, execution, evidence validation
  and linking costs separately, including reuse/skips. Grow unrelated fixture code
  while holding an isolated check constant and confirm it does not enter the local
  dependency set. Use retained preparations before expensive pilot rebuilds.
- Run appropriate targeted/public/native and repository validation using existing
  Nix infrastructure. Refresh generated registries when their inputs change;
  report pre-existing failures separately and introduce no unexplained regression.
- Provide a fresh-operator walkthrough and retained evidence mapping every G1–G6
  exit to exact commands, inputs, results and limits. Preserve unrelated changes.
  Completion requires executable demonstrations, not documentation or mocked UI.

## Scope and working discipline

G1–G4 are the first usable end-to-end checkpoint; G5 and G6 are required before
this goal is complete. Resolve concrete operation/helper/schema choices during
implementation against retained examples. Do not postpone the operator loop for
another broad design review or a collection of isolated proof primitives.

Reuse current component identities, interfaces, relations, semantic engines, work
packages, testkit and Nix storage. Add artifact boundaries only where semantics or
measured invalidation require them. Preserve proof regions versus production
components: internal cuts must preserve coverage/progress without synthetic APIs.
Tests and reviewed assumptions are not checked summaries or strong qualification.

A new GUI, automatic boundary recommendations, all oracle backends, hundreds of
components and full Hello/jq/DX-Ball lifting are outside this bounded milestone.
No commit, push or deployment is required by this plan.
All subsequent Wine launches must use an isolated headless Wayland desktop, as
requested by the operator on 2026-09-15.

## Historical completed milestone: reusable caller composition

## Previous completed milestone: independent component demonstration

The small hand-defined Metapad network milestone is complete under its explicit
trusted runtime contracts. The [requirement-by-requirement audit](baselines/2026-09-14-independent-component-milestone.md)
records the four real authoring components, original/C proofs, checked memory and
control transport, actual public edit/repair/refinement workflows, meaningful
neighboring implementation reuse, and separately validated runtime premises.
Both consumers reuse unchanged proof models when the resource implementation
changes; withdrawing EDI preservation invalidates only the UI consumer.

Current readers validate all public baseline/error/repair/neighbor and refinement
artifacts without process or model/header execution. Their exact Nix/compiler
inputs and source bindings are audited. All 659 production Python modules match
the public experiment snapshot. Fifteen native tests pass, including the current
actual maximum-width allocation-failure test; 27 retained local tests have current
inputs. Four repository gates pass, with the same two pre-existing boundary-test
failures and seven unchanged size offenders recorded separately.

This completes the conditional independent-work demonstration, not general
boundary-driven composition or strong qualification. Runtime contracts remain
trusted and locally proved application behavior remains conditional; fixture-owned
image/stack translation, arbitrary callbacks/nonreturn and full caller reachability
are not universally qualified. General split/merge, richer contracts, representation
changes, unrelated-target reuse and the Hello/jq/DX-Ball/native-link/export/portability
path continue in the broader plan. No automated boundary recommendation or native
activation is authorized by this result. Earlier checkpoint text below is historical.

Resource/notice integration (2026-09-14, v120): the existing consumer runtime
fixture now reaches ordinary-C resource retrieval and actual MessageBoxA through
both original caller slices and their ordinary-C consumers. Fifteen cases run on
both sides. The normal and loop-edit resource bodies are byte-identical to the
public proof inputs; their generated interface headers also match. Nine native
allocation/image-reference bodies match the production renderer exactly.

The retained original PE is mapped using SEC_IMAGE. LoadStringA reads its real
resource 31, and the dialog check observes the current text, caption, flags, IDOK
return and ordered resource/message/focus effects. The native namespace uses the
actual mapped base and the four original section origins. The fixture translates
between retained operation addresses and the actual mapping; raw memory and stack
admission remain fixture-owned. It checks resource coordinates, current bytes and
native address transport, then rejects the saved image reference after unmapping
and removal from admission. This does not qualify arbitrary relocation, same-base
reload generations, loader initialization or general callback/nonreturn behavior.

The first source-binding audit rejected use of the older generic resource fixture
as evidence for the public implementation. Runtime validation now uses the exact
normal and loop-edit sources instead. The two consumer proofs remain importable
with process/model/header generation forbidden (6.963s and 7.400s); the 27 retained

## Immediate milestone: a real hand-defined component network (2026-09-13)

The operator reset the goal around genuine independence. Use retained Metapad
inputs to demonstrate meaningful application components with a loop, allocation
or mutable shared memory, multiple calling contexts and multi-level composition.
Each local proof must use its own original behavior and explicit dependency
contracts, with neighboring implementation bodies absent. Check caller/adapter
compatibility separately. Do not make another large-model solver experiment a
prerequisite for implementing this boundary.

refinement through the public workflow. A requalified neighbor that preserves its
complete contract must leave the consumer proof reusable without recompiling its
model or solving it again. An incompatible contract change must identify and
invalidate affected consumers. Inspect actual model contents and build dependencies,
measure the complete edit cycle, and retain exact implementation/evidence binding.
Conditional runtime contracts require independent validation; bounded checks,
path witnesses, isolated proof adapters and source-only frame theorems do not
satisfy the real application-correctness milestone. Boundary recommendations
remain manual. Strong network, pilot, native-link, export and portability exits
remain longer-term requirements, not prerequisites for this demonstration.

## Objective

Prove a definition or connected definition set written as ordinary Portable-C
behaviorally equivalent to the exact generated Behavioral-C implementation,
without enumerating complete paths or forcing source into a synthetic
`init`/`step`/`finish` API. Carry that proof through exact provider objects and
one strong linked dispatch registry before any candidate can execute.

The detailed proof and activation contract is
[`portable-c-contextual-bisimulation.md`](portable-c-contextual-bisimulation.md).

Implementation now follows
[`independent-portable-lifting-plan.md`](independent-portable-lifting-plan.md):
demonstrate decomposition, local memory contracts and neighboring-proof reuse
before expanding component counts. After the design checkpoint below, validate the
expressiveness and implemented semantics of **hand-defined boundaries**. The
[boundary acceptance cases](independent-portable-lifting-plan.md#hand-defined-boundary-acceptance)
govern prerequisite work: representation, transport, local proof and composition
must each be demonstrated, including rejection cases. Automated boundary
recommendations are deferred. This changes sequencing, not proof authority or
the retained real-network, public-workflow and pilot exits.

The counterexample exposes a contract/adaptor mismatch before scratch creation:
the original accepts a current terminated span within the input object, whereas
the source length adapter requires the final byte of its full-capacity view to
be zero. Its service failure produces a null scratch view while the original

readers require the shared decoder in the consuming adapter's implementation
closure. Nullable operation parameters/results, state, nested records and callback
types remain closed pending their own admission and reconstruction rules.

The preceding batch implemented allocation-instance projection:

The preceding batch added explicit variable-size allocation extents:

Variable-size allocation authority now has an explicit `extent_mode:
instance_remainder` in the existing object-rule format. It is admitted only for
allocation/resource locators with the corresponding lifetime. The rule's positive
`extent` is the required minimum; the canonical reference extent is the checked
live range size minus its locator offset. Omitting the mode preserves fixed-size
semantics and existing fixed-rule payloads/hashes. A base address alone cannot
realize a dynamic extent in the Python diagnostic API.

The native plan carries the mode into its generated table, and the shared
native/proof resolver compares offsets, requested access, one-past pointers and
reference metadata against the selected instance's extent. Distinct live
allocations of one class can have different sizes. Release and address reuse
preserve generation expiry even when the replacement allocation is smaller.
Missing producer bindings still block the native plan, and the normal proof
harness still rejects unqualified runtime locators, including the new mode.

The preceding origin-record batch separated physical storage from identity:

different interior offsets, does not consume additional capacity.

The public `expert semantic-diagnose --view callers` command now inventories

external trial's files and SDK pin remain unchanged. The caller-origin proof
still needs to connect the existing runtime allocation/frame lifetime machinery
to the incoming views; the query itself does not discharge that obligation.

Typed proof service adapters now realize borrowed input references through the

call. This is a conservative termination witness, not first-NUL length semantics
or a caller-lifetime proof. Wider strings remain unsupported by this adapter.
Both receipt readers require `typed_service_borrowed_inputs_checked`; old

Metapad still needs caller-origin, target, output and callback contracts, and

Static caller leads retained alongside the checks identify the count frame's

Service transcripts now compare public memory at the call boundary using one

Machine replay and typed source replay both check the recorded observation;

included, while private-cell contracts remain separate. The comparison is
conservative over all public memory; narrowing it to checked callee footprints,
plus pointer lifetime/permissions, output effects and reentrancy, remains work.
Continuation calls are still rejected pending those contracts. Both receipt

memory assertion coverage, superseding earlier qualification receipts.

Affected validation passes in 197.08 seconds, with generated metadata refreshed.

The kernel32/windowing profiles now contain ABI-only argument-frame declarations

Continuation-dependent providers now declare a separate, unowned `exact_context`

These local proofs remain non-authorizing until their exact continuation

They also reject the predecessor that checked the old window before ESP moved.

receipt without them. Captured access methods are now compared with a protected

65 and 66 authored properties in 70 and 71 queries, but is now superseded by

and element width must reconstruct at each cut. A count-view permission mutation
that previously passed now fails explicitly at `scan:line_count`; both readers
reject inventories missing the metadata assertion. The unchanged draft's latest
10-second-budget checks pass entry but time out on scan memory equality; an

at `scan:line_count`. The next canonical extent and caller-ownership relations

in 74 queries and scan with 70 in 75, retaining the measured 30-second per-query
budget. Both readers reject omitted context assertions and predecessor evidence.
Attempt sixteen is now superseded by required canonical extent transport and
full-reference memory checks. Final attempt eighteen satisfies entry with 71
authored properties in 76 queries and scan with 72 in 77. Requested, reference
and visible extents reconstruct under the current logical origin policy,
including NUL aliases, outgoing range admission and terminating bytes in both
worlds. Shrinking the count view and its callback context together is rejected;

This is direct diagnostic evidence, with production limits unchanged. It preserves

The proof-world renderer now has an opt-in shared stack-span operation and an

2026-09-05 roadmap execution began with a frozen source baseline and a pinned
Metapad 3.6 unfamiliar-application trial. See

A new adversarial CBMC fixture reproduced connected replay accepting different
input bytes with equal event counts. The implementation now inventories an
independent input-memory equality goal using a pre-call arbitrary-byte snapshot,
including private storage exposed by logical references/views. This is a
transitional soundness repair; body-free summary composition, required pilot

The post-boundary-check pilot rebuild completed and its receipts were reopened:
jq remains qualified; Hello is violated at the connected input relation for

The exact adapter constructs a fresh seven-byte span at address 4149283, while

Connected fixed/value-bounded views now validate the requested range and realize
the incoming reference before resolving the callee's checked view. The adapter
rebuilds byte/span access contexts at that address and preserves strict summary
metadata equality. The proof world records issued reference metadata and rejects
forged bounds, missing permissions, foreign domains, stale generations, malformed
nulls, and invalid offsets; registry capacity is an asserted proof bound. Known

Hello input property passes a diagnostic replay in 86.57 seconds with these
changes. Focused world/region tests and both affected-validation passes succeed.
The fresh pre-policy-field provider build completed in 826.31 seconds: Hello's
connected input check passes, but its final `program_name` observable times out;
jq's typed call fields at position one also time out. Each is a 300-second limit,
not a counterexample, and both resulting qualifications are incomplete. Origin
records have subsequently been separated from the public-memory/event world
structure to avoid changing that structure's layout in unrelated proofs; 21
focused tests and affected validation pass after this adjustment. The final-policy
rebuild finished in 770.54 seconds: Hello still has two 300-second exit
value/observable timeouts, and jq still has a typed-call-fields timeout. Neither
qualification is complete. This remains the flat proof-world reference model;
heap/lifetime platform contracts remain unfinished.

A further adversarial solver fixture exposed an undeclared exact public write
being accepted at operation exit when declared results matched. Every exit now
requires effective public-memory equality, and the independently validated

and cannot authorize the current policy.

The first body-free strategy handles stateless, service-free scalar operations.
Supplementary source certificates prove an empty write frame and equal results
for equal scalar inputs across independent contexts. Reachable undefined bodies,
loops, and recursive calls reject this initial acyclic strategy. The connected
provider path requires the qualified exact/source dependency and binds the
certificate to its actual source, interface, headers, symbols, and profile before
omitting the callee body. Paired wrappers retain input-memory and argument checks
and share an arbitrary result. The certificates are not independent authority.
Nine focused tests pass, including actual GOTO-body absence, mismatched-input
rejection, and stale-source/certificate mutations. The first real scalar child
certificate passed. The real connected-parent build finished in 256.01 seconds;
its qualification remains incomplete because both shards violate the scan
invariant. The trace gives zero input bytes nonzero abstract lower-case results
(128 in the entry shard, 161 in the sync shard), so the abstraction admits
continuing beyond a NUL terminator. The next summary increment needs a checked
postrelation; assuming zero preservation without proving it would be unsound.
Receipt-bound diagnostic GOTO reconstruction confirms both the exact and source
callee bodies are absent (7,283 entry instructions and 6,467 sync instructions).
Service-free adapters now supply the runtime context needed by paired wrappers.
Affected validation passes in 150.25 seconds. These results do not complete the
real-caller or callee-size scaling exits.
Its first build exposed a cost calculator that incorrectly counted backedges to
the starting cutpoint. Cost bounds now stop at the same barriers as exact slices;
an uncut cycle still rejects. General state, effect, lifetime, exceptional-outcome,
postrelation and scalability obligations remain open.

Scalar source certificates now carry optional proved predicates in the existing
Relation IR. Zero preservation is proposed generically for single-argument scalar
operations, then checked against the actual source; false candidates leave the
weaker summary intact. The reader checks the signature and reconstructs the
predicate harness, binding compilation inputs and checker options. Twelve focused
tests pass, including false-fact rejection, rehashed-predicate/command mutations,
and a size experiment: 256 additional source statements grow the checked callee
from 4 to 260 GOTO instructions while the paired parent remains at 1,158. This
experiment is non-authorizing and does not replace real-caller qualification.
The postcondition-enabled real caller build completed in 1,308.27 seconds, and
the hardened-policy rebuild completed in 1,415.89 seconds. Both entry and sync
shards are satisfied and `ascii-string-compare` qualification is complete. The
current readers accept the latter receipt and reject rehashed missing-signature,
missing-command, and unsatisfied-fact mutations. This resolves the recorded
zero-input loop-invariant failure for the scalar caller; it does not complete
general summary composition or establish interactive latency or native activation.
Evidence is under `build/scalar-summary-contracts/checked-postrelations/`.

The scalar strategy now omits replay branches for writes, calls, and atomics
that its checked empty frame and service-free interface prohibit. Argument,
input-memory, prefix, and call-pairing checks remain. The paired size fixture
shrinks from 1,158 to 1,122 instructions and retains the constant-size result
under callee growth. Successful proofs now retain their receipt-bound C inputs
as well as failures, enabling GOTO reconstruction; those files are proof-only,
non-authorizing artifacts. Focused checks pass, and affected validation including
this retention change passes in 135.94 seconds. Both real builds completed with
qualified callers, in 1,237.76 and 1,097.36 seconds respectively. The latest receipt
has 81/82 assertion properties and passes both readers and the negative mutations.
Reconstruction from its retained inputs yields 7,236/6,420 GOTO instructions and
confirms both callee bodies are absent. The corrected inspection preserves each
region's source/header directory; the earlier hash-only selection crossed region
boundaries and is superseded. Evidence is under `effect-free-replay/` and
`retained-models/corrected-goto-inventory/` in the same hierarchy. These scalar results meet the
corresponding caller/body-absence checks; general memory/state/effect summaries,
interactive latency, the remaining pilots, and linked/native activation remain
open.

Per-query timing records and path-qualified compile-input records now accompany

rather than inlining its body; generate exact-write-specific stack-cache

Completion requires satisfied strong contextual receipts for every activated
pilot, exact linked-object/dispatch evidence in a real Portable-C candidate,
and all applicable gates. A realized derivation, passing runtime test, source
receipt, or partially satisfied shard is not completion.

# Previous Completed Goal: Faithful Semantic-Module Deployment and Incremental Idiomatic Lifting

## Historical authority note

Everything below this heading records the previous completed goal and its
2026-09-02 checkpoints; it is not the current execution contract or current
target status. That completed goal did not replace or narrow
[`unified-behavioral-c-lifting-native-ingress-deployment-plan.md`](unified-behavioral-c-lifting-native-ingress-deployment-plan.md).
Its detailed plan remains the historical specification and evidence journal.

## Objective

Implement and verify every requirement in the unified Behavioral-C lifting,
native-ingress, and deployment plan through all staged clean cuts. Deliver a
fast automatic faithful-C path for the whole conservative semantic universe
and a practical operator workflow that replaces small and medium semantic
slices with independently qualified idiomatic C. Preserve honest blockers for
jq and DX-Ball rather than manufacturing authority.

The goal is incomplete until the exact deployed candidates and observed
project distributions satisfy every required semantic, provider, runtime,
ingress, TLS, SEH, composition, deployment, observation, performance,
metadata, architecture, absence, Nix, and applicable Wine gate.

## Keystone and canonical semantic boundary

The keystone is `linked-semantic-module-v2` over
`executable-transfer-plan-v2`, with the following exact interpretation:

1. `executable-transfer-plan-v2` is the only executable semantic language.
2. `semantic-object-v1` is a content-addressed relocatable package over that
   language. It may package or reference transfer bodies, symbols, roots,
   relocations, objects, environment contracts, and provider requirements; it
   must not translate function behavior into a second semantic IR.
3. A packaged `semantic-object-v1` is the sole production input to the direct
   conservative semantic linker.
4. `linked-semantic-module-v2` records the deterministic may-realization
   universe, stable definitions, typed relocations, genuine semantic holes,
   typed residual runtime obligations, and only canonical site-local
   frontiers. It does not embed a second copy of executable semantics.
5. Whole-program must-provenance, solvers, emulators, fuzzers, CBMC examples,
   differential execution, and tests remain analysis or veto mechanisms.
   Their failure cannot remove may-reachable behavior, grant authority, or
   change production module identity.
6. Generated Behavioral C explicitly owns every original definition in the
   faithful configuration. Qualified portable providers may replace exact
   content-addressed slices in hybrid configurations. No selection may fall
   back silently.

This is one semantic language, one relocatable packaging boundary, one
production link algorithm, one total provider selection, and one native
realization/deployment chain. It is not permission to create a universal
artifact containing analysis, source presentation, runtime state, and PE
layout.

## Non-negotiable invariants

- Preserve fail-closed authority and veto-only diagnostics.
- Preserve the complete root, direct-edge, exception, outcome, relocation,
  object, and provider-requirement universes under migration and broadening.
- Distinguish semantic closure, executable qualification, and deployed
  completion in every status surface.
- Bind every selected source and object to the pinned compiler, checker,
  linker, realization, deployment, and candidate hashes.
- Keep PE layout, ingress bridges, TLS, SEH, loader surfaces, and candidate
  observation downstream of semantic linking.
- Keep generated faithful C immutable. Operator-authored C lives only in a
  separately hashed source package and qualifies only its selected slice.
- Migrate every in-tree consumer before retiring a production format, reader,
  constructor, input, command, or compatibility path.
- Prefer the existing Python implementation, Nix content-addressed phases,
  and measured algorithmic improvements. Add a dependency, cache, daemon,
  proof format, or Rust kernel only after a real vertical demonstrates that it
  is necessary.
- Tests and evaluator comparisons can veto a claim but cannot authorize one.

dropped from the outgoing bridge table, wildcard physical-frame rows competed
with exact callable targets, and saved caller state was addressed relative to
each transfer's changing input stack rather than its stable captured base.
The final gates bind one interface catalog with four methods, seven typed
indirect-callthrough obligations, all 76 site-target pairs, 71 selected
definitions, 11 runtime obligations, the preserved factory import, 17 native
bridges, the composed PE, and the observed deployment hash. The focused
runtime tests and complete native-module Wine/deployment/observation gate pass.

The binary-producing fixture remains deliberately input-addressed with fixups
disabled. Floating content-addressed finalization can rewrite an embedded
output path in PE/COFF auxiliary bytes after the fixture has hashed the exact
module, invalidating its own receipt. All semantic phases above those exact
binary bytes remain content-addressed. This is an integrity boundary, not a
second cache or semantic path.

Checkpoint (2026-09-02): callback-bearing interface callthrough is now closed
through that same generic fixture and runtime. Header-derived callback
signatures lower to checked PE32 physical frames; unsupported aggregate,
floating, wide, narrow, or unknown callback results remain fail-closed rather
than being guessed as EAX. The provider publishes an interface callback,
re-enters the candidate on the same host thread, receives the checked result,
and an invocation-lifetime callback retained past the call is rejected. Exact
object/vtable ranges created for the temporary interface instance are released
with the same generation; pre-existing ranges are reused without being
silently overwritten or released.

9,022-RVA callback target set out of 49 checked contracts into one

original contract and verifies its original digest before lowering. No target
or site-target pair is removed.

Checkpoint (2026-09-02): the factory and first COM method slices now close

The same transducer now has a conservative generic local-cell form. A cell is
accepted only at a profile-declared caller-memory argument, has 1..256 fully
initialized words, is allocated below the checked outgoing frame, and is
saved, initialized, observed, and restored transactionally. A typed
`local_cell_word` result may select only a word in that same writable cell.
The semantic contract turns every initial word into an exact machine guard
and binds the logical service result to the post-call memory projection.
Canonical calls that omit a redundant total argument-node list now use the
fixed checked ABI frame while retaining every sparse transfer stack-write
agreement. Focused parser, proof, failure, and C-renderer tests pass, and the
external renderer was split into its owning module rather than extending the
overlay monolith; both production modules are below the architecture ceiling.

This intentionally does not authorize DX-Ball's remaining descriptor calls.
The original `GetCaps` cell initializes only `DDCAPS.dwSize`; the rest is an
output region, and both `CreateSurface` calls initialize only fields selected
by `DDSURFACEDESC.dwFlags`. The pinned header AST proves pointer shape,
lifetime, and enclosing-object access, but not the read-before-write footprint
needed to replace those partial cells. Filling unspecified words with zero or
pretending the whole cell was initialized would strengthen the environment
and manufacture authority. The blocker is therefore narrowed to a reusable
profile-checked partial input/output cell contract. The authored draft has
also been corrected to use cooperative-level flag 8 and the machine
procedure's zero-on-failure/one-on-success convention; those source edits do
not reduce authority.

That is still not portable-provider authority. The two success-tail calls
clear the target-owned object table and publish the primary surface in a
target-owned global before the original epilogue returns one. The authored C
does not perform either effect. A faithful generated-C continuation is the
preferred ownership split, but this component begins inside an existing
physical stack frame. Re-entering generated C therefore requires a checked
continuation portal that proves every live register, flag, stack, object, and
lifecycle fact expected by the target unit. A jump target by itself is not
such a proof. The target-owned blocker now names
`checked_faithful_continuation_portal_state` separately from the six outcome

boundary and continues to select generated Behavioral C.

## Completion state

No work remains inside this goal. Treat the floating derivation advertisement
as a plan, not an invalidation measurement; the controlled jq probe above is
the measured gate.

Do not implement a continuation portal merely to lower DX-Ball's blocker
count. It becomes in-scope only for a future request to authorize the portable
`directdraw-init` overlay, and then it must prove the complete physical state
relation against an exact transfer-plan target. For this goal, retain explicit
generated-C ownership, the honest blocker, total provider selection, and no
silent fallback.
